chapter: First bands and the road in the South
title: Alonzo Ross's band at the Della Robia in Miami
summary: Alonzo Ross's twelve-piece band played a colored nightclub in Miami with Hall and Fulbright, and broadcast from a Miami Beach station.

story.theme_name: Coming to New York: clubs, jams, and making it
story.community_name: Making it in New York: arrival, clubs and the scene

blocks.x: Well, I'll be darned. Well, so -- all right, then, from Eagle Eye Shields, you went down to Florida, you joined Alonzo Ross.
Yeah. I was in Florida.
Oh. Oh, yeah, of course, because you were in Jacksonville.
Uh-huh.
Well, Alonzo Ross was playing where?
Alonzo Ross was playing in Miami, at
the Della Robia.
What was that? A nightclub?
A nightclub on Second Avenue down there. A colored nightclub. And Edmund Hall joined his band. And he wanted me, too. So we left Eagle Eye and went with Alonzo Ross.
Well, who else was in that band?
Uh, who else was in that band? I remember Fulbright, the bass player.
That's Fulbright that went with Chick later on, huh?
Yeah. Yeah. Fulbright. He went with Teddy Hill.
Oh.
You remember Teddy Hill. He used to wear the big hat and clown. Yeah, he went with Teddy Hill.
So he didn't go with Chick?
No.
Oh.
Him and -- who else can I remember?
Well, how many pieces were in the band?
I think he had 12.
Oh, he did?
12 pieces.
He had the sections, then.
Yeah.
So what did you play? You were playing third trumpet, huh? Or were you playing some first?
I think we only had two trumpets.
Oh, I see.
So we used to broadcast.
Oh, for goodness' sake.

Some radio station over there on the beach, Miami Beach. And that wasn't something that you heard of, because there wasn't no colored allowed over there on the beach, then. And so they used to sneak us over there to the radio station and sneak us back.
No kidding? Really?
Uh-huh. And so that's how the fellow heard us in New York. He heard the band, the fellow that owned the Rosemont Ballroom in Brooklyn.
He heard the band over the air?
Yeah. So he came down and listened to the band. So he hired the band. You know, two weeks.
No kidding.
That's how I happened to get to New York.
